text:
Priya (prod): quick sync — proposal: move from a single global token bucket to per-model-family budgets + a cheap per-tenant fast-path at the gateway. thoughts?
Marco (infra): love the idea in general. main concern is how gateway and admission talk — we currently expect a single quota check per request.
Jen (eng-runtime): can we avoid an extra roundtrip? per-model-family budgets sounds like it needs more metadata at the gateway to decide admit vs fallback.
Priya (prod): goal is reduce tail latency while still enforcing fairness across tenants and model families. gateway should short-circuit most admits using cached micro-budgets and fall back to admission svc for contested cases.
Alice (sre): what about burst fairness? customers using multiple models could game per-model buckets to get more aggregate throughput.
Marco (infra): we considered hierarchical quotas: tenant-level cap + per-model-family sub-budgets. gateway enforces a cheap decrement on the per-model-family shard; admission service enforces global tenant cap asynchronously if needed.
Noah (devex): UX question: how do we expose this to tenants? current billing and quotas are tenant-wide. Do we surface per-model budgets or keep it internal?
Priya (prod): keep it internal initially. expose metrics in Console per-tenant: effective ceiling, and per-model usage breakdown. no config surface yet.
Jen (eng-runtime): implementation sketch: gateway holds small sliding-window counters for (tenant, model-family) with TTL ~5s. admit-bot can be used for low-confidence decrements. If gateway sees counter exhausted, return provisional error with a retry-after and trigger an async check to admission.
admit-bot: AUTO: flagged pattern: "provisional-error" must map to retry behavior in SDKs (status 429 + header X-RW-Retry-After).
Marco (infra): tradeoffs: - Pro: significant reduction in p95 latency because most admits are inline. - Con: complexity in correctness; need reconciliation to avoid drift.
Alice (sre): reconciliation plan: admission service emits periodic reconciles every 30s for hot tenants and a full ledger snapshot every 5m. Gateway uses eventual correction and accepts small temporary overshoot (configurable grace).
Priya (prod): abuse vector: attacker spins many short requests across model families to exhaust tenant cap slowly. mitigation: add an abuse score that multiplies per-request cost by a penalty factor when triggered.
Jen (eng-runtime): implementation detail: request cost = tokens * model-cost-factor * abuse-penalty. Gateway can approximate using cached model-cost-factor, admission computes exact cost.
Marco (infra): interface boundary: define a compact admission protocol: CheckRequest { tenant_id, model_family, tokens_est, request_id, brief_abuse_hint } -> CheckResponse { admit: bool, tokens_allowed, definitive_cost, reconciliation_hint }. Keep it wire-friendly (small fields).
Noah (devex): can we publish a lightweight SDK change that maps provisional 429s to automatic small retries with jitter? that'll make rollout much smoother for customers.
Priya (prod): yes — Noah + DevEx own client mapping. Also add Console docs explaining provisional semantics.
Alice (sre): SLO / monitoring: add metrics for gateway-shortcircuit-rate, provisional-429-rate, reconciliation-delta. create alert if reconciliation_deltas exceed 5% over 1m for any tenant.
Marco (infra): rollout plan: 1) alpha on internal tenants with opt-in header. 2) enable for low-risk customers with read-only workloads. 3) ramp to general availability and enable reconciliation thresholds.
Jen (eng-runtime): checklist for rollout: telemetry hooks, reconciliation jobs, SDK retry support, feature flag in gateway, abuse-penalty heuristics ready.
Priya (prod): decision call: proceed with prototype this sprint. Marco/Jen to split gateway/admission proto + Noah to prototype SDK retry. Alice to draft SRE runbook. I'll create RFC follow-up doc after prototype.
Marco (infra): ack. creating PR for proto sketch.
Noah (devex): I'll add client-side retry shim and test against local admit-bot.
Alice (sre): I'll add alerting dashboard draft and postmortem template for quota drift.
Priya (prod): thanks all — tagging for visibility @here :rocket:
Noah (devex): linking a related read: https://redwood.example.com/rfc/hierarchical-quotas (internal)
Jen (eng-runtime): one more note: we should keep a deterministic fail-open parameter for emergency ops. Gateways must be able to opt into fail-open mode with strict logging.
Priya (prod): noted. we'll include that in the runbook.
Marco (infra): PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/4321 (proto sketch)
Priya (prod): moving to action items in the follow-up doc. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
